issues.legal_issue: An alienee whose acquired rights are challenged may appeal to protect those rights even if the alienor does not continue the appeal.
material_facts: The challenged gift had been made to the appellant, whose rights under it were disputed.
The alienor initially joined the appeal but later abandoned it, leaving the alienee to pursue the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The alienee was competent to prosecute the appeal to protect her rights under the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: A person who acquired rights under a challenged alienation may pursue an appeal to protect those rights; their existence does not depend on the alienor continuing to support the alienation.

predicates.appeal_challenges_an_alienation: The proceeding is an appeal in which a transfer of property is challenged.
predicates.appellant_is_alienee: The appellant acquired rights under the challenged transfer.
predicates.alienee_may_appeal: The alienee may pursue the appeal to protect the rights acquired under the transfer.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a transfer and the appellant acquired rights under it, the alienee may pursue the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A special custom relied on to establish inheritance rights cannot be considered when it was neither pleaded nor proved by the party asserting it.
material_facts: The parties admitted that the general custom entitled a widow of a predeceased son to maintenance when collaterals were present.
The respondents relied on a special custom under which the widow could inherit, but did not plead or prove that custom.
The special custom had not been raised in the pleadings or addressed by an issue in the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The special custom should not have been permitted to be raised or relied on.
issues.legal_principle: The party asserting a special custom bears the burden of pleading and proving it; the general custom described in Rattigan's Digest of Customary Law, paragraph 9, did not itself establish the asserted special custom.

predicates.special_custom_raised: A party relies on a particular custom as the basis for an asserted legal right.
predicates.special_custom_not_pleaded: The party asserting the custom did not set it out in the pleadings.
predicates.special_custom_not_proved: The party asserting the custom did not establish it with evidence.
predicates.special_custom_cannot_be_relied_on: The asserted special custom cannot be relied on to determine the parties' rights.

issues.definition: When a party raises a special custom but neither pleads nor proves it, that custom cannot be relied on.

issues.legal_issue: A mutation report stating that a person was an heir does not, without admissible evidence establishing the custom, prove that the person inherited under a special custom.
material_facts: A revenue officer's report described the widow as an heir, and a mutation in her favour was sanctioned.
The report was not evidence given in court and was not tendered to prove the special custom.
No application or other evidence showing the basis for the widow's claimed inheritance was before the court.
issues.conclusion: The report and mutation order did not prove that the widow was a customary heir.
issues.legal_principle: An official's statement or opinion about heirship does not establish the custom on which that opinion may have been based; the existence of a special custom must be proved by admissible evidence.

predicates.customary_heirship_inferred_from_mutatio: A party relies on a mutation report or order to infer that a person inherited under a custom.
predicates.records_do_not_prove_the_custom: The mutation records are not admissible evidence establishing the custom and no other evidence proves it.
predicates.mutation_records_do_not_establish_custom: The mutation records do not establish that the person inherited under the asserted custom.

issues.definition: When customary heirship is inferred from mutation records that do not prove the custom, those records do not establish customary heirship.

issues.legal_issue: An unregistered agreement cannot be used to change the character of possession that began before the agreement from adverse to permissive.
material_facts: The widow had been in possession before executing an unregistered agreement that described limited life interests and restricted alienation.
The agreement was offered to show that her possession became permissive after its execution.
Using the agreement for that purpose would make it operate to alter the character of existing possession and give effect to its terms.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was inadmissible to establish the nature of the widow's possession after its execution.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, bars using an unregistered document that requires registration to give effect to its terms. Varatha Pillai v. Jeevarathnammal (1918) was distinguishable because the person whose possession was in issue there entered into possession only after the document and claimed possession under it; here possession predated the document.

rule.if: document_requires_registration and document_is_unregistered and possession_preceded_document and document_offered_to_change_possession_character

predicates.document_requires_registration: The document contains terms that require registration to give them effect.
predicates.possession_preceded_document: The person whose possession is at issue was already in possession before executing the document.
predicates.document_offered_to_change_possession_ch: The document is offered to show that pre-existing possession later changed from adverse to permissive.
predicates.document_inadmissible_to_recharacterize_: The document cannot be admitted for the purpose of changing the legal character of the pre-existing possession.

issues.definition: When an unregistered document requiring registration is offered to change the character of possession that began before it, the document cannot be used for that purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A non-heir who possesses property adversely to the reversionary heirs without an arrangement with them acquires absolute title when that adverse possession continues for the applicable limitation period.
material_facts: The widow was entitled only to maintenance under the admitted general custom, and the asserted special custom making her an heir was not proved.
There was no evidence that she entered possession under an arrangement with the reversionary heirs.
She entered possession on the owner's death, held the lands adversely to the collaterals, and remained in possession beyond the applicable limitation period.
The gift and mortgage were made after that period had elapsed.
issues.conclusion: The widow had acquired title to the lands by adverse possession before making the gift and mortgage, and the respondents' claim failed.
issues.legal_principle: A person entitled only to maintenance is not an heir merely by possessing the property; absent an arrangement with the heirs, possession may be adverse to them and confer title after the limitation period. Bura Mal v. Narain Das was distinguishable because possession there arose under an arrangement with the heirs. Lajwanti v. Safa Chand and the related authorities concerned widows possessing as heirs, whereas the special custom that could have made the widow an heir here was not proved. The Court also referred to Sham Koer v. ... for the principle that possession by persons entitled only to maintenance is adverse to the reversionary heirs unless it results from an arrangement with them.

rule.if: reversionary_property_dispute and possessor_not_proven_heir and possession_without_arrangement and adverse_possession_continued_for_limitation_period

predicates.reversionary_property_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to property by persons asserting rights as reversionary heirs.
predicates.possessor_not_proven_heir: The person in possession has not been proved to be an heir entitled to possess the property as such.
predicates.possession_without_arrangement: The person entered or remained in possession without an arrangement with the persons claiming as reversionary heirs.
predicates.adverse_possession_continued_for_limitat: Possession adverse to the reversionary claimants continued for the applicable limitation period.
predicates.absolute_title_acquired_by_adverse_posse: The possessor acquired absolute title to the property by adverse possession.

issues.definition: In a reversionary property dispute, a non-heir possessing without an arrangement acquires absolute title if the possession is adverse and lasts for the applicable limitation period.
